x: Bill Webb was caught by Goodall, an Army runner who has just joined Mitcham, but managed to get away from his man over the final sprint and so regain our lead.

Charlie Churcher was taking a bashing but quite enjoying it and there were hopes he might catch Goodall, Woodford's 2nd man. Pat Sapcote was determinedly chasing three Woodford men and the odds seemed that he would catch them, in fact he assured us that it was in the bag, and he certainly did it.

At this point, Highgate seemed to have the team race well in hand, with Shaw not far behind Tunbridge and Brazier. The "Bels" were ahead of Woodford, who had three men well up—Cotton, Goodall and Foster—but whose fourth man (then Alf.

This race once again proved the value of our Police Walkers and, in particular, showed the rapid improvement of George Checkley, who walked an excellent race to finish 2nd to Goodall of Woodford in the excellent time of 2 hrs. 27 mins. 2 secs.

W.C., Poly H., and ourselves all scored 40 points and priority was given to the clubs who were first to finish their teams. Charlie Churcher walked exceptionally well to take individual honours, beating Goodall of Woodford Green by exactly 30 seconds.
After the 10 laps we moved out on to the road with George leading from Bryan Hawkins and myself, Bob Goodall, McFarlane, and Don Thompson with the French team.
Our confidence in Eric as the potential winner was strengthened when at 5 miles he led with Goodall of Woodford Green, a previous title holder.
